title: Compact Insight Orbit: Component Library and Accessibility Audit
creator: Ava Chen
description: Summary: Design and deliver a compact, re-usable component family called 'Insight Orbit' for small dashboard tiles, rollout indicators, and cost-summary snapshots. The family should be built as composable primitives in Figma (container, micro-chart, status-pill, affordance rail, and tokenized spacing) and include an accessibility audit and annotated guidelines for engineering handoff. Scope covers: core components, token mappings for density variants, prototype states for canary/cascade rollouts, and a brief performance-minded spec for rendering lightweight metric snapshots in constrained panels. Out of scope: full-page dashboard redesign, backend telemetry changes. Context: multiple PM/Eng requests for a smaller metric surface that can be embedded in lists, canary rollout panes, and in the cost explorer compact view. Existing token families are inconsistent across teams; this ticket consolidates and prescribes a minimal set for compact density scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: Figma component library published in the Console team space with documented variants (compact, condensed, touch) and usage notes
Token mapping sheet exported (token name -> figma variable) and approved by design lead
Accessibility audit completed: WCAG AA contrast for all color tokens, keyboard focus states documented, and screen-reader labels for each atomic component
Prototype demonstrating: (a) 3 compact dashboard tiles in a grid, (b) a rollout rail showing canary/primary/fallback states, and (c) cost snapshot that toggles between estimated/actual
Handoff checklist created with CSS token snippets, React example props, and a small PR template for Runtime/Console engineers
Design review signoffs from PM (Maya Patel) and Eng lead (Diego Rojas) recorded in comments
decisions: Use a 4px baseline spacing token set for compact variants to keep density consistent with micro-lenses
Favor semantic tokens (surface/strong/notice/warn) over hex tokens in the library to enable theming and future SSO color overrides
Adopt a single 'status-pill' component with icon, label, and optional timestamp instead of separate variants to reduce cognitive load for engineers
Micro-chart primitives use simplified sparkline SVGs that expose only color and stroke tokens for fast rendering and bundling
